newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds open weaker but outperform U.S. bonds.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds open weaker but outperform U.S. bonds.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened weaker on Thursday, pulled lower by weakness in U.S. Treasuries, but outperformed amid a stronger currency and a positive Canadian inflation report, analysts said.

"The Canadian sentiment was stronger than in the U.S. but the U.S. was weighing Canada down. The consumer price information was good in Canada, very good in fact," said Arve Bendiksrud, a fixed-income analyst with TD Securities Inc.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.22 to C$110.83 to yield 7.083 percent. The U.S. 30-year bond fell 12/32 to yield 6.91 percent.
The spread between the bonds narrowed to 17 basis points from 18 basis points at the close of trading on Wednesday.

Canadian bonds took direction from U.S. Treasuries, which were weaker following the release this morning of consumer price index data for April. Analysts said the market responded to a 0.3 percent rise in core U.S. CPI as well as fall in jobless claims.

However, in Canada the inflation picture was much brighter. Statistics Canada said the country's consumer price index less food and energy prices -- so called core CPI -- rose 1.8 percent on the year, in line with expectations.
Both the positive Canadian inflation report and strong gains in the Canadian dollar overnight helped the Canadian market to outperform, Bendiksrud said.
Canada's dollar opened stronger at C$1.3846 (US$0.7222) on Thursday as investors showed good interest to buy the unit before and after the release of Canadian inflation data.

The release of the release of the Bank of Canada's semi-annual monetary policy report this morning did not have an immediate impact on bond prices. In the report the Bank of Canada said it did not see the need for further monetary easing if the economy and inflation developed as predicted.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.07 to C$103.20 to yield 6.543 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 5/32 to yield 6.69 percent.
The negative spread between the two bonds widened to 15 basis points from 13 basis points at the close of trading on Wednesday.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 3.08 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.18 percent.
